author: GIA desk
title: Iran's seven-day plan is not new
reason: - Iran first presented it in mid-September after a temporary ceasefire collapsed, and it has received a US reply. - AP reported that Trump rejected a Tehran proposal to end the war "late last month". - Its conditions are partly public: lifting the US port blockade, cancelling oil sanctions, and a halt to fighting "on all fronts". The Supreme National Security Council speaks of seven conditions. - The sticking point is the US demand to address the nuclear programme first. - We had said the conditions were "not published". The analysis is reworded and stays possible. - Sources: Reuters via Arab News, CBS/AP live.

author: GIA desk
title: The mine claims are disputed
reason: CENTCOM says it has cleared the strait of mines and that ships are being hit by projectiles. It also says the GFS Pride was hit by an IRGC projectile, not a mine. The title and summary now say so. Source: Al Jazeera.

author: GIA desk
title: The UKMTO count depends on the outlet
reason: Al Jazeera reports at least 12 attacks in the week to Oct 16, while AP/CBS reports 10. Both call it a wartime weekly high, and the story now gives both figures. Sources: Al Jazeera, CBS.

author: GIA desk
title: Most attacks are still off Oman
reason: That is where the US escorts ships, not outside its corridor. AP says this has been true since early July. The analysis is rewritten and downgraded from likely to possible. Source: CBS/AP.

author: GIA desk
title: Egypt is a net loser from the war
reason: - Egypt's monthly gas import bill rose from about $560m to $1.65bn. The National reported this in April, so the figure is from April. - That far outweighs Suez's gain. July revenue was $505m, up from roughly $355m a year earlier. - The analysis no longer calls the corridor a "revenue lifeline" and adds The National as a source. - Sources: The National, TT/Bloomberg.

author: GIA desk
title: Sisi's "if requested" is now in the summary
reason: It was already in the title. Source: CBS.

author: GIA desk
title: The Mecca pact is not an "Arab bloc", and Egypt is not a member
reason: - Its members are Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan. Cairo says it is "seriously considering" joining. - Iran's mediation offer came on Oct 16, a day before Sisi spoke, so "designed to slow that" was dropped. - Source: Türkiye Today/Bloomberg.

author: GIA desk
title: The WSJ report is now attributed
reason: The WSJ was citing people briefed on Saudi and anti-Houthi Yemeni intelligence. Source: Iran International.

author: GIA desk
title: The Russian strike was not a reply to the waiver
reason: - Trump signed the waiver on the night of Oct 16, and the strike came the same night. - Putin had already ordered more "massive and coordinated strikes" on Oct 16. - The story now presents the two as concurrent. The analysis drops from likely to possible, and the waiver cause drops to speculative with a new "why". The old cause is kept. - Sources: ISW, RFE/RL.

author: GIA desk
title: Starshield is contested
reason: The Poland sabotage analysis now says Ukraine's Starshield service was disrupted and the reasons are contested. It no longer says access is "already being curbed". Sources: ISW, RFE/RL.

author: GIA desk
title: Cuba's grid crisis started in mid-2024
reason: - It has internal causes, an ageing grid with chronic underinvestment, and included the island-wide blackout of Oct 18–22, 2024. The US oil siege has worsened it since January. - The 75.5% figure was the forecast peak shortfall, and the deficit eased on Oct 17 (758 MW available). - The title is reworded and the analysis drops from likely to possible. - Sources: Infobae/EFE, Wikipedia, Peter's World.

author: GIA desk
title: The Brazil polls were on mixed bases
reason: - Vox's 51–49 for Lula is on valid votes. Datafolha's 47–45 for Flávio Bolsonaro was on total votes; on valid votes it is 51–49 for Bolsonaro. - Both now appear on the same basis. "Complete Latin America's right turn" is softened to "extend". - Sources: G1, Exame.

author: GIA desk
title: The Sahel citation was wrong
reason: - The Malijet link was the Oct 10 article, which gives 5,396 tankers since September. - The 734-tanker convoy of Oct 17 is in a different article, now added. The summary now says "5,396 from September to Oct 10". - Source: Malijet.

author: GIA desk
title: The Pakistan–Afghanistan citation didn't support the claim
reason: Dawn does not carry the Taliban's claim of 7 Pakistani soldiers killed. The story already cited Infobae/EFE for it, and India Today is now added. (BBC Pashto also covers the clash.) Source: India Today.

author: GIA desk
title: The settler attack on diplomats now has a source
reason: The Guardian's report from Taybeh is added. Source: Guardian.

author: GIA desk
title: The Israel polls are split
reason: - The Times of Israel poll has Eisenkot ahead with neither bloc at 61. - Channel 14 has Likud ahead (29 to 20–22) with the right-wing bloc at 61–62. I could not confirm the i24 figure, so it is not used. - Source: Channel 14.

author: GIA desk
title: DR Congo
reason: - Enquete.cd says no direct link between the Belgian raids and the freeze has been officially established, and the raids concern accusations against the First Lady and her family. - The summary now says this. The "fears defections" analysis drops from possible to speculative. - Source: Enquete.cd.

author: GIA desk
title: Taiwan
reason: MND logged 2 sorties, 5 PLAN ships and 9 official ships (MND). The story already had the 5 navy ships; the brief left them out.

author: GIA desk
title: Yasukuni
reason: the condemnation came from China's embassy in Japan, which the story already says (Xinhua).

author: GIA desk
title: MOAB
reason: the plans are prepared "if ordered by President Trump" (CBS). The story already said this; the brief's "ready" is looser.

author: GIA desk
title: Deep dive
reason: Bloomberg says the Suez recovery began earlier in the year and that the tanker rise "likely at least partly" reflects rerouting (TT/Bloomberg). The brief's "first time since 2023" overstates this. The National's gas-bill figure also makes Egypt a net loser, not a "quiet beneficiary".

author: GIA desk
title: Footer "447 stories" vs 1,454
reason: not an error. Git shows the archive held exactly 447 stories when the edition was applied at 7:07 AM ET. The 1,454 total comes from today's backfill runs, which came afterwards.

author: GIA desk
title: China's open-source exclusion
reason: the story already says open-source work is exempt. The "offshoring" alternative is a judgment call with no source given, so I left it out.

author: GIA desk
title: Ethiopia, "Getachew is aligned with Addis"
reason: I found no source that says so. The story calls him ex-Tigray leader and already reports Eritrea's denial (Frontlines.et confirms both). No change.

author: GIA desk
title: France, "only a possible link"
reason: the analysis was already labelled possible. No change.

author: GIA desk
title: "Europe will carry Ukraine's winter: likely", the diesel barrels, the Saudi events vs expat label, and the Fed hike tail risk
reason: these are in the brief only, with no story text to correct, so they are not in the packet.
